questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The country and environment was very important to me, and Scotland was the perfect fit in that regard.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, they are very helpful and experienced when helping exchange student as they have many visiting student at the University of Edinburgh.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went to talk to the visiting student office, and I wrote emails back and forth with the office as well to get answers to my questions.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I applied through the university, and it was very easy in that regard. My advice would be to be aware of deadlines and always have other options available just in case.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There might be a some distance from the university, and getting familiar with public transport and the walking path to the university is crucial.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was shocked at the prizes of the accommodation, so be aware that it might be more expensive than you are used to.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was a bit complicated with all the paperwork necessary, but that is to be expected.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The visiting student office was very helpful and answered the questions I asked, and provided advice when needed.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was not very succesful with my classes, I had apparently given them the course list incorrectly, and I therefore did not get the classes I wanted, but I ended up enjoying my classes anyway.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to reach out and ask if they have received all the paperwork needed, to make sure that everything goes as plan.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took two third year courses and a single second year course as was adviced my the visiting office. This helped a lot with settling in, but also later when writing the exam as it was somewhat easier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different, and I needed to adjust to the new style, and sometimes it worked well, but other times it was difficult to do everything required in the course. I still prefer the teaching at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Shakespeare: Modes and Genre

Contemporary Cinema

American Innocence

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed all three of my courses, but especially American Innocence, it was the course I wanted the least, but the course I enjoyed the most.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I sometimes had to pay for films for my course, but other than that, everything was pretty much expected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The housing was insanely expensive, and it shocked me just how expensive it was.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many different options, everything from salsa dancing to film club to swimming societies. There are plenty of opportunities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I did not join any societies, but I was interested in joining the film soc, and a gaming club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go and see other parts of Scotland than Edinburgh, such as Glasgow, Aberdeen and the Highlands.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy, I like the culture and the people, so it was not challenging to adjust.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Find common interests.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their kindness, it was refreshing coming from Copenhagen where people can be a bit cold.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open-minded. 

Face challenges head-on. 

Ask for help when you need it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Prepare to be challenged, but also relax, you are all in the same boat.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to attend my dream university.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The academic work, it was challenging trying to find the right rhythm.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
